title: Making a zippered scatter cushion in upholstery fabric
subtitle: Cut and stitch a square or rectangular cushion cover in upholstery-weight fabric with a concealed zip along one seam
excerpt: How to make a scatter cushion cover in upholstery fabric with a concealed zip. Covers measuring the cushion pad, cutting fabric panels, inserting the zip in the back seam, stitching the remaining seams, and turning out.
sourceNotes: Traditional soft furnishing and upholstery craft practice, public domain.

glossaryTerms.definition: The strip of fabric between the cut edge and the stitch line. For upholstery fabric a standard seam allowance is 15 mm. The total size of each cut panel is the finished dimension of the cushion face plus the seam allowance on every cut edge.

A zip whose teeth curl inward and are hidden behind the tape when the zip is closed, leaving only a thin seam line on the face. It requires a specialist concealed zip foot on the sewing machine that opens the coil as it sews, placing the stitch line right alongside the teeth. When closed, the join is almost invisible.

content.text: A scatter cushion cover with a

is a fitted fabric envelope that looks clean from all four sides. Upholstery fabric (linen, velvet, or wool blend) holds its shape better than dress fabric for cushions. BEGINNER: straight seams only; the zip is the one step to take carefully.
Measure the cushion pad. Add 15 mm
to each edge for both the front and back panels. Cut two panels of this size from the upholstery fabric. Check the grain is straight on both panels before cutting.
Insert the zip in the back seam

Place the front and back panels right sides together. The zip goes along one edge: this is the bottom edge of the cushion. Open the zip fully. Stitch the zip tape to the seam allowances of the two panels along the zip edge, using a concealed zip foot that guides the stitch directly alongside the zip coil. Close the zip and check the seam lies flat.

Open the zip halfway before stitching the remaining three seams so the cover can be turned out. Stitch the three remaining sides right sides together at 15 mm seam allowance. Clip the corners diagonally to reduce bulk. Turn the cover right side out through the zip opening, pushing the corners out fully with a blunt tool.
Insert the cushion pad and close the zip. Press the seams from the outside with a steam iron set to the fabric type, using a damp pressing cloth on velvet or pile fabrics to avoid crushing the pile.

attrs.symptom: Zip pucker shows as a ridge on the cushion face
attrs.cause: The seam allowances on either side of the zip were not equal in width, or the fabric was not pulled flat during sewing.
attrs.fix: Open the zip and re-stitch the seam more precisely alongside the zip coil. Use a stitch-unpicker to remove the original stitches and resew.

attrs.symptom: Corners of the cushion cover are bunched rather than square
attrs.cause: The seam allowance was not clipped at the corners, or the corners were not pushed out fully when turning.
attrs.fix: Turn the cover inside out, clip the corner seam allowance diagonally closer to the corner point, and turn out again.
